title: Securities and Exchange Board of India — Investor Education & Goal Planning Principles
publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
summary: SEBI principles on aligning financial horizons with asset classes, multi-goal priority scheduling, risk assessment, and systematic wealth preservation.

chunks.title: Goal Horizon Classification and Asset-Liability Matching
chunks.text: SEBI Investor Education guidelines prescribe mapping financial goals according to time horizons: Short-term goals (< 3 years, e.g. laptop purchase, emergency booster) require capital preservation in low-volatility fixed-income instruments like liquid funds and short-term bank deposits. Medium-term goals (3 to 7 years, e.g. car purchase, wedding) benefit from balanced asset allocation. Long-term goals (> 7 years, e.g. house purchase, retirement) permit growth-oriented equity asset classes.

chunks.title: Resolving Competing Goals and Priority Conflicts
chunks.text: When an individual faces concurrent goal milestones with inadequate monthly surplus, SEBI guidelines suggest strict priority ranking: (1) Mandatory risk protection (health/life insurance and emergency buffer), (2) Non-negotiable milestone goals (e.g. debt payoff, children's education), (3) Discretionary aspiration goals (e.g. luxury vacations, vehicle upgrades). Discretionary targets should undergo timeline extensions rather than compromising emergency reserves.

chunks.title: Risk Profiling and Avoidance of Speculative Over-Leverage
chunks.text: Every personal financial plan must reflect the user's risk tolerance and loss-bearing capacity. Individuals with high monthly fixed commitments, dependents, or irregular income profiles should maintain conservative asset distributions. Over-leveraging via unsecured personal loans to fund lifestyle consumption is classified as a critical financial health hazard.
